evidence.pali: ‘‘Kathaṃ bhāvitā, ānanda, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, ānanda, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī’’ti. Tatiyaṃ.
evidence.chinese_simplified: “阿难，七觉支如何修习、如何多修习，才能圆满明与解脱呢？阿难，在此，比丘修习念觉支，依于远离，依于离贪，依于灭，导向舍弃；修习择法觉支……修习舍觉支，依于远离，依于离贪，依于灭，导向舍弃。阿难，如是修习、如是多修习七觉支，便能圆满明与解脱。”第三。
evidence.english: How, Ānanda, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and liberation? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. He develops the enlightenment factor of the investigation of phenomena… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. Indeed, Ānanda, when the seven factors of enlightenment are developed and cultivated in this way, they fulfill knowledge and liberation.” The third.

entries.pali: Virāgānupassī ti ettha dve virāgā khayavirāgo ca accantavirāgo ca. Tattha saṅkhārānaṃ khayavayato anupassanāpi, accantavirāgaṃ nibbānaṃ virāgato dassanamaggañāṇampi virāgānupassanā . Tadubhayasamāṅgīpuggalo virāgānupassī nāma, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘virāgānupassī’’ti, virāgato anupassantoti attho. Nirodhānupassi mhipi eseva nayo, nirodhopi hi khayanirodho ca accantanirodho cāti duvidhoyeva. Paṭinissaggānupassī ti ettha paṭinissaggo vuccati vossaggo, so ca pariccāgavossaggo pakkhandanavossaggoti duvidho hoti . Tattha pariccāgavossaggo ti vipassanā, sā hi tadaṅgavasena kilese ca khandhe ca vossajjati. Pakkhandanavossaggo ti maggo, so hi nibbānaṃ ārammaṇaṃ ārammaṇato pakkhandati. Dvīhipi vā kāraṇehi vossaggoyeva, samucchedavasena khandhānaṃ kilesānañca vossajjanato, nibbānañca pakkhandanato. Tasmā kilese ca khandhe ca pariccajatīti pariccāgavossaggo, nirodhe nibbānadhātuyā cittaṃ pakkhandatīti pakkhandanavossaggoti ubhayampetaṃ magge sameti. Tadubhayasamaṅgīpuggalo imāya paṭinissaggānupassanāya samannāgatattā paṭinissaggānupassī nāma hoti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘paṭinissaggānupassī’’ti. Na kiñci loke upādiyatī ti kiñci ekampi saṅkhāragataṃ taṇhāvasena na upādiyati na gaṇhāti na parāmasati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatī ti aggaṇhanto taṇhāparitassanāya na paritassati. Paccattaññeva parinibbāyatī ti sayameva kilesaparinibbānena parinibbāyati. Khīṇā jātī tiādinā panassa paccavekkhaṇāva dassitā. Iti bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa saṃkhittena khīṇāsavassa pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ pucchito sallahukaṃ katvā saṃkhitteneva khippaṃ kathesi.
entries.chinese_simplified: “随观离欲者”(Virāgānupassī)，于此有二种离欲：衰灭离欲与究竟离欲。其中，随观诸行的衰灭，以及视究竟离欲的涅槃为离欲的道智，即是随观离欲。具足此二者之人，名为“随观离欲者”。就此而说“随观离欲者”，意即随观离欲。于“随观灭者”(Nirodhānupassī)亦是同理，因为灭亦有二种：衰灭之灭与究竟之灭。于“随观舍遣者”(Paṭinissaggānupassī)，此中“舍遣”被称为“舍”(vossagga)。它有二种：舍离之舍与跃入之舍。其中，舍离之舍即是观(vipassanā)，因为它暂时舍离诸烦恼与诸蕴。跃入之舍即是道，因为它以涅槃为所缘而跃入。或由二种原因而皆是舍：以根除的方式舍离诸蕴与诸烦恼，以及跃入涅槃。因此，舍离诸烦恼与诸蕴，称为“舍离之舍”；心跃入灭、涅槃界，称为“跃入之舍”。此二者皆会合于道中。具足此二者之人，因具备此舍遣随观，故名为“随观舍遣者”。就此而说“随观舍遣者”。“于世间无所执取”，即对任何一个行，不因渴爱而执取、不执持、不触取。“无所执取，故不忧恼”，即不执持者，不因渴爱而忧恼。“他于自身般涅槃”，即他自己以诸烦恼的般涅槃而般涅槃。“生已尽”等句，则显示了他的省察智。如是，世尊就天帝释所问漏尽者的前分道，浅显、简要且迅速地作了回答。
entries.english: In 'contemplating dispassion,' there are two kinds of dispassion: dispassion as destruction and ultimate dispassion. Therein, both the contemplation of formations in terms of their destruction and vanishing, and also the path-knowledge that sees Nibbāna—which is ultimate dispassion—as dispassion, are called 'contemplation of dispassion.' A person endowed with both of these is called 'one who contemplates dispassion.' It is with reference to that person that 'contemplating dispassion' is said; the meaning is 'one who contemplates in terms of dispassion.' In 'contemplating cessation' also, this is the same method; for cessation is also twofold: cessation as destruction and ultimate cessation. In 'contemplating relinquishment,' relinquishment (paṭinissagga) is called letting go (vossagga), and that is of two kinds: letting go as abandonment and letting go as plunging into. Therein, letting go as abandonment is insight; for it lets go of defilements and aggregates by way of substitution of opposites. Letting go as plunging into is the path; for it plunges into Nibbāna as its object. Or, it is letting go for two reasons: because of letting go of the aggregates and defilements by way of cutting off, and because of plunging into Nibbāna. Therefore, because it abandons defilements and aggregates, it is 'letting go as abandonment'; because the mind plunges into the Nibbāna-element through cessation, it is 'letting go as plunging into.' Both of these converge in the path. A person endowed with both of these is called 'one who contemplates relinquishment' because of being endowed with this contemplation of relinquishment. It is with reference to that person that 'contemplating relinquishment' is said. 'He does not cling to anything in the world' means: he does not cling to, does not grasp, does not misapprehend even a single thing included in formations by way of craving. 'Not clinging, he is not agitated' means: not grasping, he is not agitated with the agitation of craving. 'He personally attains Parinibbāna' means: he himself attains Parinibbāna through the Parinibbāna of defilements. By 'Birth is destroyed,' etc., his reviewing knowledge is shown. Thus, when asked by Sakka, the lord of the devas, about the preliminary practice of one whose taints are destroyed, the Blessed One, making it simple, spoke briefly and quickly.

entries.pali: 255 . Sattame yena gilānasālā tenupasaṅkamī ti ‘‘sadevake loke aggapuggalo tathāgatopi gilānupaṭṭhānaṃ gacchati, upaṭṭhātabbayuttakā nāma gilānāti bhikkhū saddahitvā okappetvā gilāne upaṭṭhātabbe maññissantī’’ti ca ‘‘ye tattha kammaṭṭhānasappāyā, tesaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathessāmī’’ti ca cintetvā upasaṅkami. Kāye kāyānupassī tiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ parato vakkhāma. Aniccānupassī ti aniccataṃ anupassanto. Vayānupassī ti vayaṃ anupassanto. Virāgānupassī ti virāgaṃ anupassanto. Nirodhānupassī ti nirodhaṃ anupassanto. Paṭinissaggānupassī ti paṭinissaggaṃ anupassanto.
entries.chinese_simplified: 255. 第七经中，关于‘前往病房’：[世尊]思惟：‘于天人世间，身为最上之人的如来亦前往看护病人之处，[如此]比丘们将会信受、决意，认为“病人确实是应受照料者”’，并且思惟：‘我将为那里适合修习业处的[比丘]们说示业处’，因此而前往。关于‘于身随观身’等句，所应说者，我等将于后文解说。‘随观无常’，即随观无常性；‘随观坏灭’，即随观坏灭；‘随观离欲’，即随观离欲；‘随观灭’，即随观灭；‘随观舍遣’，即随观舍遣。
entries.english: 255. In the seventh [sutta], regarding the passage 'he approached the sick hall,' he approached thinking: "Even the Tathāgata, the foremost person in the world with its devas, goes to attend to the sick. The monks, having believed and accepted this, will consider that the sick are to be attended to." And also: "For those there for whom a meditation subject is suitable, I will teach a meditation subject." What should be said regarding 'contemplating the body in the body,' etc., that we will speak of later. 'Contemplating impermanence' means contemplating the state of impermanence. 'Contemplating vanishing' means contemplating vanishing. 'Contemplating dispassion' means contemplating dispassion. 'Contemplating cessation' means contemplating cessation. 'Contemplating relinquishment' means contemplating relinquishment.

entries.pali: Aniccānupassī ti aniccato anupassanto. Virāgānupassī ti ettha dve virāgā khayavirāgo ca accantavirāgo ca. Tattha saṅkhārānaṃ khayaṃ khayato passanā vipassanāpi, accantavirāgaṃ nibbānaṃ virāgato dassanamaggañāṇampi virāgānupassanā. Tadubhayasamaṅgipuggalo virāgānupassī nāma. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘virāgānupassī’’ti, virāgato anupassantoti attho. Nirodhānupassimhi pi eseva nayo. Nirodhopi hi khayanirodho accantanirodhoti duvidhoyeva. Paṭinissaggānupassī ti ettha paṭinissaggo vuccati vossaggo. So ca pariccāgavossaggo pakkhandanavossaggoti duvidho hoti. Tattha pariccāgavossaggo ti vipassanā. Sā hi tadaṅgavasena kilese ca khandhe ca vossajati. Pakkhandanavossaggo ti maggo. So hi nibbānaṃ ārammaṇato pakkhandati. Dvīhipi vā kāraṇehi so vossaggoyeva, samucchedavasena khandhānaṃ kilesānañca vossajanato nibbāne ca pakkhandanato. Tasmā kilese ca khandhe ca pariccajatīti pariccāgavossaggo. Nirodhāya nibbānadhātuyā cittaṃ pakkhandatīti pakkhandanavossaggoti ubhayampetaṃ magge sameti. Tadubhayasamaṅgī puggalo imāya paṭinissaggānupassanāya samannāgatattā paṭinissaggānupassī nāma hoti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Na kiñci loke upādiyatī ti kiñci ekampi saṅkhāragataṃ taṇhāvasena na upādiyati na gaṇhāti na parāmasati. Anupādiyaṃ na paritassatī ti aggaṇhanto taṇhāparitassanāya na paritassati. Paccattaṃyeva parinibbāyatī ti sayameva kilesaparinibbānena parinibbāyati. Khīṇā jātī tiādinā panassa paccavekkhaṇā dassitā. Iti bhagavā saṃkhittena khīṇāsavassa pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ pucchito saṃkhitteneva kathesi. Idaṃ pana suttaṃ therassa ovādopi ahosi vipassanāpi. So imasmiṃyeva sutte vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā arahattaṃ pattoti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 随观无常者，即随观为无常。随观离欲者，于此有二种离欲：灭尽离欲与究竟离欲。其中，观诸行(saṅkhāra)之灭尽为灭尽的观(vipassanā)，以及以道智见究竟离欲之涅槃(nibbāna)为离欲，皆是随观离欲。具足此二者之人，名为随观离欲者。针对此而说‘随观离欲者’，其义为‘随观为离欲’。于随观灭者，亦复如是。灭亦实有二种：灭尽之灭与究竟之灭。随观舍遣者，于此，舍遣被称作‘弃舍’。此弃舍有二种：遍舍之弃舍与跃入之弃舍。其中，遍舍之弃舍即是观，因其以支分舍的方式弃舍诸烦恼(kilesa)与诸蕴(khandha)。跃入之弃舍即是道(magga)，因其以涅槃为所缘而跃入。或由于二种原因，道亦是弃舍：以正断的方式弃舍诸蕴与诸烦恼，以及跃入涅槃。因此，因其遍舍诸烦恼与诸蕴，故为‘遍舍之弃舍’；因心为寂灭而跃入涅槃界，故为‘跃入之弃舍’。此二者皆会遇于道中。具足此二者之人，因其成就此随观舍遣，故名为随观舍遣者。针对此而说。‘于世间无所执取’者，即不因贪爱(taṇhā)而执取、不执持、不谬执任何一行法。‘不执取则不忧恼’者，即不执持，故不因贪爱之忧恼而忧恼。‘唯独于内寂灭’者，即自己以烦恼之寂灭而寂灭。以‘生已尽’等句，显示其省察。如是，世尊(bhagavā)被问及漏尽者(khīṇāsava)之前分道(pubbabhāgappaṭipadā)，便以简略的方式开示。此经对长老(thera)而言，既是教诫，亦是观。他于此经中增长观，证得阿罗汉果(arahatta)。
entries.english: ‘Contemplating impermanence’ means one who contemplates as impermanent. Regarding ‘contemplating dispassion’: Here, there are two kinds of dispassion: dispassion as destruction and absolute dispassion. Therein, both the seeing, which is insight, of the destruction of formations as destruction, and the path-knowledge that sees Nibbāna, the absolute dispassion, as dispassion, is the contemplation of dispassion. A person endowed with both is called one who contemplates dispassion. With reference to this, it is said, ‘one who contemplates dispassion,’ meaning one who contemplates as dispassion. The same method applies to ‘one who contemplates cessation.’ For cessation is also twofold: cessation as destruction and absolute cessation. Regarding ‘one who contemplates relinquishment’: Here, relinquishment is called letting go (vossagga). And it is twofold: letting go by abandoning (pariccāgavossagga) and letting go by plunging into (pakkhandanavossagga). Herein, letting go by abandoning is insight (vipassanā). For it lets go of both defilements and aggregates by way of substitution. Letting go by plunging into is the path. For it plunges into Nibbāna as its object. Or, it is called letting go for two reasons: because of letting go of aggregates and defilements by way of cutting off, and because of plunging into Nibbāna. Therefore, because it abandons defilements and aggregates, it is letting go by abandoning. Because the mind plunges into the Nibbāna-element for the sake of cessation, it is letting go by plunging into. Both of these come together in the path. A person endowed with both, being furnished with this contemplation of relinquishment, is called one who contemplates relinquishment. With reference to this, it is said. ‘He does not cling to anything in the world’ means: he does not cling to, does not grasp, does not misapprehend even a single conditioned thing by way of craving. ‘Not clinging, he is not agitated’ means: not grasping, he is not agitated with the agitation of craving. ‘He is personally fully extinguished’ means: he himself is fully extinguished with the full extinguishment of defilements. By ‘Destroyed is birth,’ etc., his reviewing knowledge is shown. Thus, the Blessed One, having been asked in brief about the preliminary practice of one whose cankers are destroyed, spoke in brief. Moreover, this discourse was both an exhortation and insight for the Elder. He, having developed insight in this very discourse, attained Arahantship.

entries.pali: ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… nibbānaṃ mābhinandī’’ti ayaṃ desanā. ‘‘Idha, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti, evañcetaṃ, devānaminda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti ‘sabbe dhammā nālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti, so sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so tāsu vedanāsu aniccānupassī viharati, virāgānupassī viharati, nirodhānupassī viharati, paṭinissaggānupassī viharatī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.390) imāya desanāya saṃsandati. ‘‘Yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ…pe… abhisambuddhoti vadāmī’’ti ayaṃ desanā ‘‘sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako…pe… sappurisadhamme suvinīto rūpaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati, vedanaṃ…pe…, saññaṃ…pe…, saṅkhāre…pe…, viññāṇaṃ ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Yampi taṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā, tampi ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. Yampi taṃ diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ, so loko so attā so pecca bhavissāmi ‘nicco dhuvo sassato api pariṇāmadhammo sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassāmī’ti, tampi ‘netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti samanupassati. So evaṃ samanupassanto na paritassatī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.241) evamādidesanāhi saṃsandatīti, ayaṃ catubyūho hāro .
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘诸比丘，即使是那位比丘……乃至……不应乐喜涅槃’，此为一教说。此教说与‘天帝释(Devānaminda)，在此，有比丘听闻：“一切法皆不应执取。”天帝释，既然该比丘如此听闻：“一切法皆不应执取”，他便证知一切法；证知一切法后，他遍知一切法；遍知一切法后，无论他感受到什么受——乐受、苦受或不苦不乐受——他都于那些受中安住于随观无常、随观离贪、随观灭、随观舍遣’（《中部》1.390）相连结。‘诸比丘，即使是那位阿罗汉比丘……乃至……我说他是正自觉者’，此为一教说。此教说与‘诸比丘，多闻的圣弟子……于善士法善受调伏，他审察色：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”他审察受……想……行……识：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”任何所见、所闻、所觉、所得、所寻求、为意所寻思者，他也审察：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”任何见的立足处，即“世界即我，我死后将是常、恒、久、不变易之法，我将如是永恒存续”，他也审察：“这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的我。”如此审察，他便不忧虑’（《中部》1.241）等教说相连结。此为四严饰导引(catubyūho hāro)。
entries.english: “Even that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus… should not delight in Nibbāna,” this is the teaching. This connects with the teaching: “Here, O lord of devas, a bhikkhu has heard: ‘All things are not fit for clinging.’ When a bhikkhu has heard thus, ‘All things are not fit for clinging,’ he directly knows all things. Having directly known all things, he fully understands all things. Having fully understood all things, whatever feeling he feels—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—he dwells contemplating impermanence in those feelings, contemplating dispassion, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment.” (MN 1.390) “Even that bhikkhu, O bhikkhus, who is an arahant… I declare him fully enlightened,” this is the teaching. This connects with such teachings as: “But the instructed noble disciple, O bhikkhus… well-trained in the Dhamma of the noble ones, regards form thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ He regards feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ And whatever is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, and examined by the mind—that too he regards thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ And even that standpoint of views: ‘This world is the self; after death I shall be permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, I shall remain the same for ever and ever’—that too he regards thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Thus regarding, he is not agitated.” (MN 1.241) This is the fourfold guide.

entries.pali: Uppādavayaṭṭhenā ti udayabbayasabhāvena uppajjitvā nirujjhanena. Aniccā ti addhu vā. Aniccalakkhaṇaṃ aniccatā udayavayatā. Tasmā ti yasmā pañcannaṃ khandhānaṃ khayato vayato dassanañāṇaṃ aniccānupassanā, taṃsamaṅgī ca puggalo aniccānupassī , tasmā. Khayavirāgo ti khayasaṅkhāto virāgo saṅkhārānaṃ palujjanā. Yaṃ āgamma sabbaso saṅkhārehi virajjanā hoti, taṃ nibbānaṃ accantavirāgo. Nirodhānupassimhipī ti nirodhānupassipadepi. ‘‘Eseva nayo’’ ti abhidisitvā taṃ ekadesena vivaranto ‘‘nirodhopi hi…pe… duvidhoyevā’’ ti āha. Sabbāsavasaṃvare vuttavossaggova idha ‘‘paṭinissaggo’’ti vuttoti dassento ‘‘paṭinissaggo vuccati vossaggo’’ tiādimāha. Pariccāgavossaggo vipassanā. Pakkhandanavasena appanato pakkhandanavossaggo maggo aññassa tadabhāvato. So ti maggo. Ārammaṇato ti kiccasādhanavasena ārammaṇakaraṇato. Evañhi maggato aññesaṃ nibbānārammaṇānaṃ pakkhandanavossaggābhāvo siddho hoti. Pariccajanena pakkhandanena cāti dvīhipi vā kāraṇehi . Sabbesaṃ khandhānaṃ vossajjanaṃ tappaṭibaddhasaṃkilesappahānena daṭṭhabbaṃ. Cittaṃ pakkhandatī ti maggasampayuttaṃ cittaṃ sandhāyāha. Ubhayampetaṃ vossajjanaṃ. Tadubhayasamaṅgī ti vipassanāsamaṅgī maggasamaṅgī ca. ‘‘Aniccānupassanāya niccasaññaṃ pajahatī’’tiādivacanato (paṭi. ma. 1.52) yathā vipassanāya kilesānaṃ pariccāgapaṭinissaggo labbhati, evaṃ āyatiṃ tehi kilesehi uppādetabbakhandhānampi pariccāgapaṭinissaggo vattabbo, pakkhandanapaṭinissaggo pana magge labbhamānāya ekantakāraṇabhūtāya vuṭṭhānagāminivipassanāya vasena veditabbo, magge pana tadubhayampi ñāyāgatameva nippariyāyatova labbhamānattā. Tenāha ‘‘tadubhayasamaṅgī puggalo’’ tiādi.
entries.chinese_simplified: “以生灭义”(uppādavayaṭṭhena)是指以生起后即坏灭的生灭自性。“无常”(anicca)即“非恒常”(addhuva)。无常相即无常性，是生灭的状态。“因此”是说：因为见到五蕴的毁坏与消逝之智是无常随观(aniccānupassanā)，具足此智的个体(puggala)是无常随观者，所以这么说。“灭尽离贪”(khayavirāgo)是指名为“灭尽”的离贪，即诸行的败坏。依靠它而能完全离于一切诸行者，即是涅槃，是究竟的离贪。在“灭随观者”(nirodhānupassī)的词条中也是如此。在指示“此理亦然”后，又部分地阐释说：“灭亦有……乃至……两种。”为了表明在“一切漏的防护”中所说的“舍离”(vossagga)在此处被称为“断舍”(paṭinissagga)，而说“断舍即是所谓的舍离”等。以舍弃方式的舍离是观(vipassanā)；以跃入并致力于它的方式的舍离是道(magga)，因为其他(法)没有此(功能)。“那”即是道。“作为所缘”是指通过把(涅槃)作为所缘来完成其作用。这样，除了道以外，其他以涅槃为所缘的(法)没有跃入的舍离，此理即成立。(舍离)通过舍弃与跃入这两种原因。一切蕴的舍离，应理解为断除与它们相关的烦恼。“心跃入”是指与道相应的心。这两种都是舍离。“具足此二者”是指具足观与道。根据“以无常随观舍断常想”等(《无碍解道》1.52)的文句，正如通过观可以获得对烦恼的舍弃断舍，同样，对于未来将由那些烦恼产生的诸蕴，也应说有舍弃断舍；而跃入的断舍，则应理解为通过在道中获得的、作为决定性原因的、导向出起的观。在道中，此二者都是理所当然的，因为是无保留地获得的。因此说“具足此二者的个体”等。
entries.english: “By the meaning of arising and passing away” means by the nature of arising and dissolving, by arising and ceasing. “Impermanent” means not lasting. The characteristic of impermanence is impermanence, arising and passing away. “Therefore” means: since the knowledge of seeing the decay and passing away of the five aggregates is the contemplation of impermanence, and the person endowed with it is one who contemplates impermanence, therefore. “Dispassion through decay” means this is dispassion designated as decay, the crumbling of formations. That on account of which there is complete dispassion towards all formations is Nibbāna, the ultimate dispassion. “Even in the contemplation of cessation” means also in the term ‘contemplation of cessation.’ Having indicated, “This is the method,” he explains it in part, saying: “For cessation, too … is twofold.” Showing that the relinquishment (vossagga) mentioned in the context of the restraint of all taints is here called “abandonment” (paṭinissagga), he says: “Abandonment is called relinquishment,” and so on. The relinquishment by giving up is insight. The relinquishment by plunging in is the path, because of its applying itself by way of plunging in, and because of the absence of this in anything else. That is the path. “As an object” means because of making it an object by way of accomplishing its function. For in this way it is established that, apart from the path, there is no relinquishment by plunging in for other things that have Nibbāna as their object. “By giving up and by plunging in” means or by both these reasons. The relinquishing of all the aggregates should be seen as the abandoning of the defilements connected with them. “The mind plunges in”: he says this referring to the mind associated with the path. Both these are relinquishment. “One endowed with both” means endowed with both insight and the path. From the statement, “Through the contemplation of impermanence, one abandons the perception of permanence,” etc., just as through insight the abandonment by giving up defilements is obtained, so too the abandonment by giving up the aggregates that would be produced by those defilements in the future is to be understood. The abandonment by plunging in, however, is to be understood by way of the insight leading to emergence, which is obtained in the path and is the exclusive cause. But in the path, both are obtained by right method, being obtained directly. Therefore, he said: “The person endowed with both,” etc.

entries.pali: Āgamanīyapaṭipadā ti ariyamaggassa āgamanaṭṭhāniyā pubbabhāgapaṭipadā. Pubbabhāgāyeva na lokuttarā. Sampajaññaṃ pubbabhāgiyameva. Tisso anupassanā pubbabhāgāyeva vipassanāpariyāpannattā . Missakā ti lokiyalokuttaramissakā. Bhāvanākālo dassito ‘‘nirodhānupassino viharato, paṭinissaggānupassino viharato rāgānusayo pahīyatī’’ti vuttattā.
entries.chinese_simplified: “趣向道”，是作为趣向圣道之处的前分行道。这只是前分，而非出世间。正知也只是前分。三种随观也只是前分，因为它们属于观的范畴。“混合”是指世间与出世间的混合。修习的时间已说明，因为经中说：“安住于随观灭、安住于随观舍时，贪随眠即被断除。”
entries.english: 'The way of approach' is the preliminary practice that is the place of approach to the noble path. It is preliminary, and not supramundane. 'Clear comprehension' is preliminary. The three kinds of contemplation are preliminary, because they are included within insight. 'Mixed' means mixed mundane and supramundane. The time for cultivation is shown, for it was stated: "When one dwells contemplating cessation, dwells contemplating relinquishment, the underlying tendency to lust is abandoned."

entries.work_title: 阿毗达摩入门-名色分别 Abhidhammāvatāro-Nāmarūpaparicchedo
entries.pali: Tato virāgānupassī, nibbinditvā virājayaṃ; Tathā nirodhānupassī, bhūmidhamme nirodhayaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于是观离贪，厌离而离染；同样地，观止灭，止灭诸地法。
entries.english: Then, contemplating dispassion, having become disenchanted, one causes fading away; likewise, contemplating cessation, one causes the phenomena of the planes to cease.
